title: All Spain Here, Distant and Mine
text:
All Spain here, distant and mine,

inhabiting, dreamed and true,

the doubt and faith of the passing soul,

all dawn and also all agony.

Beautiful, yes, beneath the light without day

that gives her to me by the sea, alone and whole:

field of serene spring

that hides its sweet and late flower.

Grave Spain, still in hope,

made of time and of my time, Spain,

faithful land of my life and of my death.

You are this blood and this force

of love that grows impatient and accompanies

the faith and doubt of seeing you again.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Spain as both distant homeland and intimate blood, faith, doubt, and return.

title: Epitaph of the Beloved in the Lover's Voice
text:
Buried beneath a mute willow,

her pure presence is not stone and silence;

I find her in the wings of your voice, secure

with life and death in a loving knot.


Her light raises your sharp cry,

and in it her happy tenderness nests,

filling the flowered height with joy

and the naked orchard with tears.


All your word is born from her pulse,

all your earth trembles and lives

from being the earth where her form lies.


Your fulfilled being receives from her yesterday

this bleating that grazes on her lips,

present grass that tomorrow writes.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the epitaph's strange pastoral ending: bleat, grazing lips, present grass, future writing.

title: Nostalgia for First Love
text:
Your solitude of leaning snow,

virginal and simple, in my memory,

like faithful water from a weary waterwheel,

comes to irrigate my enamored voice.


How the quiet soul recreates

the half-light and sweetness of that story,

with gleams of late glory,

constellated among bees and fruits!


O delicate flame, first ardor

veiled in weeping and celestial gaze,

equal to the trill, the fountain, and the lily!


Look at me, embattled and imprisoned,

returning to your brief and broken illusion

like a trembling in the deserted sand.
editorial_note: The translation keeps first love as snow, waterwheel, bees, late glory, and broken illusion.

title: It Is Leaving Me Almost Without Entrails...
text:
This tremendous love raised high

is leaving me almost without entrails,

-O wasteland of expanded ardors!-

where I hear my voices as though strange.


Make my blood serene in the intimate

cabins of your being and your care,

and keep me in the enamored air

with which at times you deceive my pain.


If my flame hurts you, O clear fountain,

I will erase the moist cloudbanks

that your eyelids warmly kindle.


I will return their landscapes to your skies,

nailing deep into your eyes

the gentle orchards of my savage ardor.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's paradoxes: raised love, clear fountain, gentle orchards, savage ardor.

title: Come to My Sweet Riverside Fields
text:
Come to my sweet riverside fields

that sigh in poplars to see you.

Toward the breeze your breath pours out,

the meadow will lift its grasses.


Spring will be thick with flowers

when it wakes beneath the weight of your dream.

From the roots of death will rise

the wings of the life that waits for you.


The waters of the foam of your bath

will open like lips, like shores,

to kiss the light in your stature.


And now that you shine only with imminence,

look in my heart, year after year,

at the world full, and the hours on their knees.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the invitation's river landscape, death-rooted life, and kneeling hours.
